title: Wine Wimsey Review · Thu Nov 26
subtitle: NEW-VOICE test batch 4. Replaces the earlier old-style 7+2 Nov 26 batch.json; those PNGs remain in this folder. 8 character feed posts + 2 stories. All posts use the locked cartoon character with a rotating expression and an action. Captions and first comments included. No TOBIs, no plain cards. Seasonal: #01 (Black Friday), S1 (Christmas sale emails). Four then-vs-now story cards in slots 2, 4, 6, 8 after a stats-based swap (pharmacy and plumber replaced reply-all and movie talkers). Quotes: 10 original. Credits: GenerateImage (free). Scott accepted all 8 feed posts and 2 stories and said upload on Nov 25. First-comment delays randomized (1-20 minutes). Posting time blank so posts fill Scott's staggered Post Planner queue slots.

posts.quote: Black Friday used to be one day. / Now it starts November 1st, / and the 'sale' price is what it cost in August.
posts.caption: I watched a coffee maker go from $79 to $119 in October, then 'down' to $89 for the big sale. I'm not a math teacher, but I know that's not a deal.
posts.first: I'm doing my shopping in January this year. Whatever's left is what they're getting.
posts.alt: Cartoon illustration of a woman with dark wavy hair, a grey streak, and black glasses in a store entrance, a blue glow around her. She rolls her eyes and holds up a blank sale flyer like evidence, shopping carts and a BLACK FRIDAY SALE sign behind her. Text at the top reads: Black Friday used to be one day. Now it starts November 1st, A pink box at the bottom reads: And the 'sale' price is what it cost in August.
posts.note: new-voice batch 4, approved via upload Nov 25
posts.expression: slow eye-roll, holding the sale flyer up like evidence

posts.quote: In 1983 the phone rang and it was somebody you knew. / Now it's my car's extended warranty. / I sold that car in 2019.
posts.caption: Back then you picked up on the first ring because it might be your mother. Now an unknown number rings and I let it go to voicemail like it owes me money.
posts.first: My sister calls from a new number every couple of years. She's been sent to voicemail more than the robots.
posts.alt: Cartoon illustration in two panels. 1983: a smiling younger woman in a blue shirt talks on a beige curly-cord phone. Now: a woman with dark wavy hair, a grey streak, and black glasses squints with her mouth open at a phone that says SPAM LIKELY. Text at the top reads: In 1983 the phone rang and it was somebody you knew. Now it's my car's extended warranty. A teal box at the bottom reads: I sold that car in 2019.
posts.note: new-voice batch 4, approved via upload Nov 25
posts.expression: young-her laughing on the curly-cord wall phone; now: open-mouth 'are you kidding me' squint at the SPAM LIKELY call

posts.quote: The rental car wanted $15 a day for a toll pass. / My whole trip had one toll. / It was $1.50.
posts.caption: The guy at the counter said it was 'for my convenience.' Then he slid over a second form for the fuel plan and a third one for the insurance I already have.
posts.first: I paid that toll in quarters like it was 1994. Felt fantastic.
posts.alt: Cartoon illustration of a woman with dark wavy hair, a grey streak, and black glasses in a rental car office, an orange glow around her. She pulls her glasses down her nose, side-eyes a rental contract, and a clerk stands behind the counter with a set of keys. Text at the top reads: The rental car wanted $15 a day for a toll pass. My whole trip had one toll. An orange box at the bottom reads: It was $1.50.

posts.quote: In 1984 Mr. Hendricks at the drugstore had your prescription ready before you found your purse. / Now I got a text that said 'ready,' waited 40 minutes in line, / and it wasn't.
posts.caption: Mr. Hendricks kept a jar of root beer barrels by the register and asked how your mother's hip was doing. Last week I typed my birthday into a kiosk three times and it still didn't know me.
posts.first: I finally got my pills the next afternoon. The text said 'ready' again, and that time I didn't believe it.
posts.alt: Cartoon illustration in two panels. 1984: a smiling younger woman digs in her purse as an older pharmacist hands her a bag. Now: a woman with dark wavy hair, a grey streak, and black glasses grimaces, holding up a phone that says READY, stuck in line. Text at the top reads: In 1984 Mr. Hendricks at the drugstore had your prescription ready before you found your purse. Now I got a text that said 'ready,' waited 40 minutes in line, A red box at the bottom reads: And it wasn't.

posts.quote: My receipt had a 4% "kitchen appreciation fee." / I thought that's what the prices were for. / Just put it on the menu.
posts.caption: The burger was $16, the fries were extra, and then this little fee showed up at the bottom in gray print like it was hoping I wouldn't see it. I saw it.
posts.first: I still tipped the waitress. It isn't her fault the owner has ideas.
posts.alt: Cartoon illustration of a woman with dark wavy hair, a grey streak, and black glasses, shown close up on an orange dotted background. She grins tightly with a stress vein on her forehead and holds up a long receipt with one line circled in red. Text at the top reads: My receipt had a 4% "kitchen appreciation fee." I thought that's what the prices were for. A red box at the bottom reads: Just put it on the menu.

posts.quote: In 1981 you bought a couch and it outlasted the dog, the kids, and two moves. / Now it's $1,400 and ships in a box, / and sags by spring.
posts.caption: My parents' plaid couch weighed as much as a car and nobody ever sank into a dip. Mine came with an Allen wrench and a permanent dent in my favorite spot.
posts.first: That plaid couch is still at my cousin's house. Still ugly, still perfect.
posts.alt: Cartoon illustration in two panels. 1981: a smiling younger woman sits proudly on a brown plaid couch. Now: a woman with dark wavy hair, a grey streak, and black glasses looks unimpressed, pressing into a sagging gray cushion next to an open shipping box. Text at the top reads: In 1981 you bought a couch and it outlasted the dog, the kids, and two moves. Now it's $1,400 and ships in a box, A purple box at the bottom reads: And sags by spring.

posts.quote: You waited behind eleven cars at the drive-thru. / You saw the menu the whole time. / Why are we just now deciding?
posts.caption: Nine minutes in line, and he gets to the speaker and asks what's good. Sir, it's the same menu it's been since before you got your license.
posts.first: I ordered a Diet Coke and a small fry. I was done at that speaker in four seconds.

posts.quote: In 1984 my dad called a plumber named Earl, and Earl showed up that afternoon. / Now the app gave me an 8-to-12 window next Tuesday. / It's 3:15. Brayden is 'on his way.'
posts.caption: Earl charged my dad $40, drank two cups of coffee, and fixed the dripping bathroom faucet on his way out for free. My service call fee alone is $129, and that's before anybody touches a pipe.
posts.first: There's a bucket under my sink and a beach towel on the floor. Brayden, if you're reading this, I'm still home.
posts.alt: Cartoon illustration in two panels. 1984: a smiling younger woman holds a coffee mug while a plumber works under the sink with a leak bucket. Now: a woman with dark wavy hair, a grey streak, and black glasses smirks, glasses pulled down, tapping a tracking map on her phone.
